applied.problem: The rule of thumb 'same loads ... three times the power' holds only for fixed impedances; a loaded motor's power is set by its mechanical load. The mistake line calls cos φ an angle, and φ + 30° is true only for a matching pair (L1 current with L1–L2 voltage), not any line pair.
Screen 11's 6.8 kW hint calls 400 × 20 × 0.85 'one phase's worth', but one phase's worth is about 230.9 × 20 × 0.85 ≈ 3.9 kW; 6.8 kW is the single-phase formula applied to line values.
'Fifty times a second' is UK mains only; the course notes ships mostly run 60 Hz, and Dan will read this card in a naval context.
